newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says German inflation remains favourable.
newsitem.headline: Buba says German inflation remains favourable.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that German inflation developments remained favourable in the winter months, saying stronger inflation data in January partly reflected special factors.
"Price developments were favourable at the turn of the year 1996/97," the bank said in its February monthly report.

"It is true that consumer prices in January rose 1.8 percent on an annual basis -- somewhat stronger growth than in the whole 1996 year -- but this was partly due to factors which only had a temporary effect."
The central bank cited examples such as a rise in prices for heating oil and somefood due to bad weather.
It said there were still no signs of inflation building up in the economy.
"The rise in import prices linked to the dollar increase and the higher crude oil pries on world markets has been offset by falling domestic unit wage costs," it added.
